SCI Scenario / What-If Analyzer

Source: R/scenario.R
sci_scenario.Rd

Recomputes the Submission Confidence Index for one or more caller-specified hypothetical changes to the evidence and returns a tidy comparison against the baseline: the baseline SCI, each scenario's SCI, the delta, the band movement, and which indicators drove the change. Use it to answer "what is the highest-leverage fix to raise our readiness score?" purely mechanically.

Usage

sci_scenario(evidence, scenarios, config = sci_config_default())

Arguments

evidence

A validated evidence data.frame (from r4subcore).

scenarios

A single edit data frame, or a (optionally named) list of edit data frames. See Details for the edit-frame contract.

config

An sci_config from sci_config_default(). Pass a profile configuration here for authority-calibrated weights and bands.

Value

A list of class "sci_scenario" with:

  • baseline: a list with sci, band, gated, gate_reason, n_critical

  • comparison: a tibble, one row per scenario, with scenario, baseline_sci, scenario_sci, delta_sci, baseline_band, scenario_band, band_changed, gated, n_indicators_changed, and n_rows_changed

  • drivers: a tidy tibble of the indicators whose earned points moved, with scenario, indicator_id, indicator_name, indicator_domain, baseline_earned, scenario_earned, and delta_earned, ordered within each scenario by delta_earned descending

  • config: the configuration used

Details

Each scenario describes hypothetical edits to the evidence - for example "if indicator Q1 flips from fail to pass" or "if these findings were resolved". Every edit is caller-supplied: this function invents no weights, thresholds, or scores. It only applies the requested edits to a copy of the evidence and re-runs the existing scoring engine (compute_pillar_scores() then compute_sci()) on the modified table, so the scenario SCI is produced by exactly the same math as the baseline.

A scenario is a data frame of edits with a required indicator_id column and at least one of the scoring-input columns result and severity. For each edit row, every evidence row carrying that indicator_id has the supplied result and/or severity overwritten (an NA leaves that field unchanged). The modified evidence is re-validated with r4subcore::validate_evidence(), so an invalid result or severity value raises an error rather than being scored silently.

scenarios may be a single edit data frame (treated as one scenario named "scenario") or a named list of edit data frames (one named comparison per element; unnamed elements are labelled scenario_1, scenario_2, ...).

The drivers reuse sci_decompose(): each indicator's change in earned SCI points (scenario_earned - baseline_earned) is reported, so the drivers of a scenario sum to its delta_sci up to the usual one-decimal rounding. This makes "which items drove it" an exact accounting of the move, not a heuristic ranking.

See also

sci_what_if() for a single-indicator score override, sci_decompose() for the earned-points accounting the drivers reuse, and compute_sci() for the underlying score.

Examples

ctx <- suppressMessages(r4subcore::r4sub_run_context("STUDY1", "DEV"))
ev <- suppressMessages(r4subcore::as_evidence(
  data.frame(
    asset_type = "validation", asset_id = "ADSL",
    source_name = "pinnacle21",
    indicator_id = c("Q1", "Q2", "T1", "R1", "U1"),
    indicator_name = c("Missing var", "Label", "Trace", "Risk", "Guide"),
    indicator_domain = c("quality", "quality", "trace", "risk", "usability"),
    severity = c("high", "low", "medium", "high", "low"),
    result = c("fail", "pass", "warn", "fail", "pass"),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  ),
  ctx = ctx
))

sc <- sci_scenario(
  ev,
  scenarios = list(
    fix_quality = data.frame(indicator_id = "Q1", result = "pass"),
    fix_both    = data.frame(
      indicator_id = c("Q1", "R1"), result = c("pass", "pass")
    )
  )
)
sc
#> 
#> ── SCI scenario analysis ──
#> 
#> ℹ Baseline SCI 30.6 / 100   Band "high_risk"
#> 
#> ── fix_quality 
#> • SCI 35 (+4.4)
#> • Q1 (quality): +4.38 SCI points
#> 
#> ── fix_both 
#> • SCI 41.2 (+10.6)
#> • R1 (risk): +6.25 SCI points
#> • Q1 (quality): +4.38 SCI points
sc$comparison
#> # A tibble: 2 × 10
#>   scenario    baseline_sci scenario_sci delta_sci baseline_band scenario_band
#>   <chr>              <dbl>        <dbl>     <dbl> <chr>         <chr>        
#> 1 fix_quality         30.6         35         4.4 high_risk     high_risk    
#> 2 fix_both            30.6         41.2      10.6 high_risk     high_risk    
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: band_changed <lgl>, gated <lgl>,
#> #   n_indicators_changed <int>, n_rows_changed <int>
